name: Round-trip climb of the walk to a current stop, median (m)
group: Infrastructure · Climb on the walk to a stop (USGS 3DEP)
plain: How much the walk to the nearest bus or train stop with a current timetable typically climbs, going and coming back, for the people who live within a 400 m walk of one.
definition: The median, weighted by residents, of the round-trip climb (the sum of the rises and falls) of the walk along mapped roads from each block within a 400 m walk of a current stop to its nearest one. In meters.
geography: 78 municipalities and Puerto Rico; also 901 barrios (values only where residents live within a 400 m walk of a current stop)

coverage.frequency: Rebuilt with the nightly transit refresh, only when the walkers or the heights change.

method: climb.py takes the 2020 census blocks within a 400 m walk along mapped roads of a stop with a current timetable on 2026-10-29 (the rule of access.py: 4,914 blocks, 405,841 residents, the same as the published 'within a 400 m walk'), traces each block's shortest walk to its nearest current stop (walknet.nearest_paths) and reads the ground's height every 10 m along the roads (USGS 3DEP, interpolated between the four nearest cells), from the road nearest the block to the stop. The round-trip climb is the sum of the rises and falls; a walk is steep when a 30 m stretch rises or falls more than 1 in 12. 99 walks whose block or stop is on no walkable road are read along the straight line, as access.py measures them. A block counts whole in the barrio the crosswalk gives it; the median is weighted by residents. Checks at every build: the residents add up to the published walkers; Puerto Rico's median between 0 and 30 m; Barranquitas, Jayuya and Orocovis above it; Cataño and Toa Baja below it.
source_detail: USGS 3D Elevation Program, 1/3 arc-second (about 10 m) seamless DEM, tiles USGS_13_n18w066_20260722.tif, USGS_13_n18w067_20260722.tif, USGS_13_n18w068_20260722.tif, USGS_13_n19w066_20260722.tif, USGS_13_n19w067_20260722.tif, USGS_13_n19w068_20260722.tif; walks along mapped roads (roads.bin) to the stops with a current timetable on 2026-10-29 (transport.json, operators.json); 2020 census blocks.
how_to_read: Puerto Rico: 3.4 m. Highest: Arroyo (29.7 m), Orocovis (20.6 m), Jayuya (11.6 m). 29 municipios have residents within a walk of a current stop.
caveats: Only the residents within a 400 m walk of a stop with a current timetable are counted: in most municipios few or none are, so most areas have no value.
Heights are of the bare ground at about 10 m: a road on a bridge or an embankment reads the valley or the slope below, and a short steep stretch can be smoothed out.
Mapped roads only: steps, sidewalks and footpaths are not on the map, and a block's walk starts at the road nearest its point, not at a door.
Where few residents live within a walk, one block moves the figure a lot.

name: Walks to a current stop with a stretch steeper than a ramp may be (%)

group: Infrastructure · Climb on the walk to a stop (USGS 3DEP)
